items.stem: What is the core principle of IFRS 15?

options.text: Recognise revenue to depict the transfer of goods or services for the consideration expected
options.rationale: Correct: revenue reflects the transfer of promised goods/services at the amount expected in exchange.

options.text: Recognise revenue when cash is collected
Recognise revenue evenly across the financial year
options.rationale: Timing follows transfer of control, not the calendar.

options.text: Recognise revenue only at year end
options.rationale: Recognition follows satisfaction of obligations throughout the period.

items.explanation: Correct: revenue reflects the transfer of promised goods/services at the amount expected in exchange.

items.stem: Which TWO criteria indicate revenue should be recognised over time? (Select TWO)

options.text: The customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefits as the entity performs
options.rationale: Correct: this is one of the over-time criteria in IFRS 15.

options.text: The entity's performance creates an asset with no alternative use and there is an enforceable right to payment
options.rationale: Correct: this combination also triggers over-time recognition.

options.text: The customer pays a deposit up front
options.rationale: A deposit does not by itself determine timing.

options.text: The contract spans more than one accounting period
options.rationale: Duration alone does not mandate over-time recognition.

items.explanation: Correct: this is one of the over-time criteria in IFRS 15.

items.stem: When a contract has variable consideration, how is it treated in the transaction price?

options.text: Estimated and included, subject to the constraint that a significant reversal is not probable
options.rationale: Correct: variable consideration is estimated and constrained to avoid probable significant reversals.
IFRS 15 requires estimation, not deferral until certainty.

options.text: Always recognised at the maximum possible amount
Recognised only after the contract ends
options.rationale: It is estimated during the contract, subject to the constraint.

items.explanation: Correct: variable consideration is estimated and constrained to avoid probable significant reversals.
